![What is Design Thinking? — updated 2026 | IxDF](https://api.dataforseo.com/cdn/i/10081734-2633-0066-0000-68b08b6bf44c:4)
Design thinking is `a human-centered, iterative approach to solving complex problems by focusing on what people truly need`.[[1]](https://online.hbs.edu/blog/post/what-is-design-thinking)[[2]](https://www.nngroup.com/articles/design-thinking/)

### Core Pillars

- **Desirability:** What people actually want and need.
- **Feasibility:** What is technically and operationally possible.
- **Viability:** What makes sense as a sustainable model or business.[[1]](https://www.ideou.com/pages/design-thinking)


---

### The 5 Phases

1. **Empathize:** Learn about the people you are designing for through observation and interviews.
2. **Define:** Analyze your research to build a clear, actionable problem statement ("How Might We...").
3. **Ideate:** Brainstorm a wide range of creative, wild solutions without immediate judgment.
4. **Prototype:** Build low-cost, tactile models or sketches to give your ideas a physical form.
5. **Test:** Put your prototypes in front of real users, gather feedback, and learn what works.[[1]](https://mitsloan.mit.edu/ideas-made-to-matter/design-thinking-explained)[[2]](https://www.nngroup.com/articles/design-thinking/)[[3]](https://www.ama.org/marketing-news/the-5-phases-of-design-thinking/)[[4]](https://www.instagram.com/reel/DQ_yeGDjz6F/?hl=en)[[5]](https://www.ideou.com/pages/design-thinking)


---

### Key Characteristics

- **Non-linear:** You will often jump back and forth between phases as you learn new information.
- **Action-oriented:** You learn by making and testing rather than just talking.
- **Embrace ambiguity:** It helps teams navigate uncertainty when the path forward is unclear.[[1]](https://www.ideou.com/blogs/inspiration/what-is-design-thinking)[[2]](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Tvu34s8iMZw&vl=en&t=30)[[3]](https://designthinking.ideo.com/)[[4]](https://www.ideou.com/pages/design-thinking)[[5]](https://www.ama.org/marketing-news/the-5-phases-of-design-thinking/)

You can learn more about frameworks and methodology options through the [Nielsen Norman Group](https://www.nngroup.com/articles/design-thinking/) or [IDEO Design Thinking](https://designthinking.ideo.com/).[[1]](https://designthinking.ideo.com/)[[2]](https://www.nngroup.com/articles/design-thinking/)If you have a specific project in mind, tell me:

- What **problem or challenge** are you trying to solve?
- Who is your **target audience**?

I can help you map out an **Empathy** or **Ideation** exercise to get started.
